sections.html:
Manassas sits in Northern Virginia as a small independent city, and Prince William County uses it as the county seat. The two are separate governments. Manassas Park is the neighboring independent city. Within 9.9 square miles live 44,332 people by the 2025 estimate, up from 42,772 in 2020.

No county office touches your house here. Assessing is the Commissioner of the Revenue's job, billing and collecting is the Treasurer's, and both answer to the city. A seller therefore works with one set of city counters.

The older core of Manassas is ringed by a lot of 1980s construction. Roughly 35 percent of the housing stock dates to 1980 through 1989, the city's busiest growth decade. Those houses are around 40 years old now, which is about when roofs, furnaces, air conditioners and water heaters start asking for replacement.

Homeowner vacancy was only 0.7 percent in 2020, so good houses move. A dated one is another story. Lender-backed buyers send an inspector who writes up every worn part, and the sale can stall on that list. Cash buyers price the wear in and keep going.

Old Town Manassas is the historic center, and it hosts First Friday events on the first Friday of each month. The city also keeps 260 acres of parkland. Manassas Regional Airport lies inside the city limits, and it is the busiest general aviation airport in Virginia.

These are details a buyer can picture. When you describe your house, name the street's distance to Old Town, a park or the station. Specifics like these tend to make a cash offer more confident, because the buyer can judge how easily the property rents or resells later.

State Routes 28, 234 and 234 Business run through town, while I-66 and US 29 pass nearby without entering the city limits. The train station is shared by Virginia Railway Express and Amtrak and also holds the city's visitor center.

  • VRE commuter service stops here.
  • Amtrak's Cardinal, Northeast Regional and Crescent all call at Manassas.

Commutes average about 34.7 minutes against 28.2 for Virginia as a whole. About 73 percent of workers drive alone and 4 percent ride transit. Living near the station or a main route is a selling point, so lead with it.

Manassas bills real estate tax twice a year, on a fiscal year that begins July 1. The Commissioner of the Revenue sets assessed values and the Treasurer takes the payments.

PaymentDue dateOffice
First installmentDecember 5Treasurer
Second installmentJune 5Treasurer
Assessment of real propertyFiscal year begins July 1Commissioner of the Revenue

The Treasurer's Real Estate Tax page lays out the process. Collection questions go to 703-257-8241, and the office is at City Hall, 9027 Center Street.

Homeowners whose lender runs an escrow account usually never write the tax check themselves, because the mortgage company does. The Treasurer sends no duplicate to the owner. If a bill lands in your mailbox anyway, hand it to the lender.

Before you pick a closing day, confirm whether the current installment has gone out and who sent it. The settlement statement should then show the year split between you and the buyer, one line for each side.

People aged 65 or older, and some disabled residents, can apply for exemption or deferral through Tax Relief. A call to the Treasurer tells you whether you fit.

Accounts that fall behind can go to a collection firm. Virginia law is blunt on one point: a bill that never reached you does not cancel the penalty and interest. Owing back tax does not block a sale, though. The balance comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the Treasurer can quote the payoff.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works, step by step
sections.html:
Same state rules, one less party. Nobody lends, nobody appraises for a lender, and no inspection-driven repair list comes back to you.

  • Collect your deed, recent tax bills and any payoff letters.
  • Describe the house and say when you need to be done.
  • Choose a settlement company to search title and draw up the papers.
  • Settle on a closing day and sign.

You set the pace, and the house goes over in its current state, boxes and all if need be.

sections.h2: Closing costs on the seller's side
sections.html:
The big state charge falls on the seller: a grantor tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value. A contract may hand it to the buyer, but absent that language it is yours. Recording also requires the sale price to appear on the deed's first page.

Ask the settlement company for numbers in writing early. If you suspect a city rule touches your lot, call City Hall before you sign anything.

sections.h2: What to bring when you start
sections.html:
One folder speeds everything. Put in the deed if you can find it, the last two tax bills, payoff letters for any mortgage or lien, and a line about who lives in the house. A rented house adds the lease. Shared ownership adds the name and city of every heir.

Then tour the place as a stranger would. Jot down how old the roof, the furnace or heat pump and the water heater are, since buyers ask about those before anything else. Repairs are not required. The list simply gets you a straighter quote. Photos of each room and the mechanical equipment help too, particularly if you live far away and cannot meet anyone at the door.

sections.h2: What happens between offer and closing
sections.html:
Once you say yes, the settlement company combs the records for liens, unpaid taxes and anything else that could cloud the title. A back tax balance gets paid from your proceeds. Then you sign, the company records the deed, and your money arrives. No underwriter sits in the middle, so the contract date is normally the closing date.

Out-of-state owners can often sign remotely through the settlement company. Mention that at the start so the packet is prepared that way. Tenants, locked rooms and utilities left on until the final day are worth flagging as well, because they affect who needs a key and when.

A traditional listing in Manassas asks you to prepare the house, host showings, negotiate after the inspection and wait for the buyer's loan to clear. It can bring a higher price for a house in good shape when you have time. A cash sale gives up some of that in exchange for speed and certainty.

Whichever way you lean, line the options up on one sheet: what you would net, how long each takes, and which repairs you would pay for first. Include the tax installment, any payoff and the grantor tax so the comparison is honest.

If the house is a rental, ask whether the tenant can stay through closing. If it is inherited, ask who has authority to sign. Both answers change the timeline more than the price does.

Four situations account for most calls.

  • An 1980s house whose systems are wearing out.
  • A rental with tenants in place or repairs put off.
  • An inherited house with heirs scattered across states.
  • Escrow and tax loose ends that must be squared away at the table.

Selling directly lets you pick the date and skip the punch list. Most callers just want a firm answer about timing, so ask for one in writing and compare it to what a listing would realistically take.

faqs.q: Is Manassas the same as Prince William County?
faqs.a: No. Manassas is an independent city and also the county seat of Prince William County. The two governments are separate.

faqs.q: When are Manassas real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: December 5 and June 5. The fiscal year starts July 1.
The Commissioner of the Revenue sets assessed values, and the Treasurer collects the tax.

faqs.q: I have an escrow account. Who pays my Manassas tax bill?
faqs.a: Your mortgage company usually does. If you receive a bill, send it to your lender, since the Treasurer does not mail owners copies.

faqs.q: Do I pay a transfer tax when I sell a Manassas house?
faqs.a: Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of value. The seller pays it unless the contract puts it on the buyer. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.
